title: Doubly Protected Estimation for Survival Outcomes Utilizing External Controls for Randomized Clinical Trials
summary: Arm-marginal censoring weights fail under allowed arm-dependent censoring; exact identity repair supplied, broader efficiency and selection questions remain outside certification.

problems.claim: Theorem3.4(a) identifies arm-specific survival using pi_1^C=P(C>=t|X,R=1)
problems.location: PDF p3 Thm3.4; p12 A.1; code R/srEC_Surv.R27-34,62-71
assumptions: R Bernoulli1/2; trial A Bernoulli1/2 randomized
Potential event times Exp1 in both sources
Independent conditional censoring Exp1 in trial controls, Exp3 in treated arm
All Assumptions3.1-3.3 and finite-time censor positivity satisfied
problems.check: Correct event survival e^-t; printed IPCW equals 2(e^-t-atan(e^-t)); t=.5 gives .1226460717641 vs .6065306597126.
problems.result: Core identification formula false under its literal defined censoring nuisance.
problems.counterevidence: Appendix A.1 uses correct arm-conditional denominator; simulations have censoring hazard independent of A; caller can include A in actual censoring predictor list.
problems.impact: Major on stated identification and dependent unrestricted theoretical claims; no clinical or simulation score refuted.
problems.correction: Condition censoring survival on A and use trial-conditional treatment propensity; iterated-expectation proof supplied. Full EIF/asymptotics not re-certified.

independent_verification.original_claim_and_location: Read and visually checked original physical p3 Assumptions3.1-3.3 and Theorem3.4(a); reread AppendixA.1 p12, core EIF dependence p4, simulation censoring hazard p6 and R/srEC_Surv.R lines27-34,62-71.
independent_verification.operative_assumptions: Constant X, randomized trial A, source probability1/2 and treatment probability1/2; identical Exp(1) potential event times across sources, with independent arm-conditional Exp(1)/Exp(3) censoring. This meets exchangeability, source/control comparability, and conditional independent censoring. All needed tail probabilities are strictly positive at finite times; continuous times avoid tie conventions. AssumptionA.1 is not a premise of Theorem3.4.
independent_verification.decisive_check: New independent calculation: the treated-arm expectation cancels source/treatment weights and is integral_t^infinity 2exp(-3y)/(1+exp(-2y))dy. Substitution u=exp(-y) gives 2(u-atan(u)); at t=.5 this is 0.12264607176409958 rather than 0.6065306597126334. At t=0 it is2-pi/2, so normalization itself fails. The report deliberately grants the trial-conditional interpretation of the treatment propensity; no unmentioned marginal-A premise is needed for this contradiction.
independent_verification.alternatives_and_counterevidence: A.1 uses an arm-conditional censoring survival in its final line, consistent with a conditioning omission; simulations set censoring hazard independent of A. Static code confirms censoring predictors omit A by default but callers can add it. These prevent an empirical-failure conclusion, but do not make the explicit p3 formula true over its stated domain.
independent_verification.core_dependency_and_severity: Retain Major on the stated identification formula and reliance of the unrestricted integrative theory on that formula. No patient-level conclusions, reported clinical estimates or simulated scores are refuted.
independent_verification.repair_scope: For continuous event/censor times, E[1(C>T)/G_a(T,X)|T,X,A=a,R=1]=1; trial treatment weighting then gives the correct survival. Replacing G by G_a changes the formula; assuming C independent of A given X,R instead narrows the model. Neither establishes the complete revised EIF/asymptotic theory.
independent_verification.ancillary_scope_check: The report does not elevate the nuisance-rate or selection concerns to separate proved theorem failures. Independently, zero nuisance error cannot remove the empirical sampling term; and integrating the stated exponential mixture gives equal RMST with mixture weight 0.5634084559217304 while the curves differ. The latter is correctly excluded as a counterexample to Assumption3.3.
